extracted.intended_audience: Early career researchers and research administrators at U.S. universities, DOE national laboratories, and Office of Science user facilities (potential applicants to the DOE Early Career Research Program)
extracted.subtask_short: DOE Early Career Research Program application
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application (pre-application and, if invited, full application) to the Department of Energy Office of Science Early Career Research Program (FY2023), meeting eligibility, topical, and deadline requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant position/affiliation eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for the program, a researcher must be an untenured, tenure-track assistant or associate professor at a U.S. academic institution or a full-time employee at a DOE national laboratory or Office of Science user facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core eligibility criterion — applicants must hold one of the specified positions/affiliations. Implicitly excludes tenured faculty, non-DOE part-time lab staff, and non-U.S. institutions unless they meet the listed categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility window extension (COVID-19 accommodation)
rubrics_metrics.description: To address special circumstances and challenges due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Office of Science is extending the eligibility window for this competition from 10 to 12 years for all applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should apply the extended 12-year window when determining their eligibility; consult the program announcement for exact calculation (e.g., from degree date or other baseline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic fit / eligible research topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Early career researchers may apply to one of eight Office of Science program offices: Advanced Scientific Computing Research; Biological and Environmental Research; Basic Energy Sciences; Fusion Energy Sciences; High Energy Physics; Nuclear Physics; Accelerator R&D and Production; and Isotope R&D and Production. Proposed research topics must fall within the programmatic priorities of DOE’s Office of Science, which are provided in the program announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must align with the specific program office priorities listed in the official program announcement; applicants should select the single appropriate office and ensure topic fit to avoid desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding levels and award duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards to an institution of higher education will be approximately $875,000 over five years and awards to a DOE national laboratory average approximately $2,500,000 over five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget planning should reflect the stated approximate totals and five-year duration. Note the higher lab average and the stated intent to raise university funding to encourage increased graduate student stipends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation regarding graduate student support
rubrics_metrics.description: The funding level for institutions of higher education has been raised to encourage these institutions to increase graduate student stipends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: University applicants should consider allocating increased stipend support for graduate students in their budgets, consistent with the program's expressed goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process: mandatory pre-application and invitation-only full applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-applications are mandatory and are due on Thursday, January 5, 2023, at 5:00 p.m. EST. Applications will be due on Thursday, March 23, 2023, at 11:59 p.m. EST. Only those applicants that receive notification from DOE encouraging a formal application may submit full applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the required pre-application by the stated deadline; only invited applicants may submit full proposals by the full-application deadline. Failure to submit a pre-application or missing deadlines will disqualify you from the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection mechanism: competitive peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding will be competitively awarded on the basis of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare proposals to meet the standards of peer review (clarity of intellectual merit, feasibility, qualifications, environment, etc. as detailed in the program announcement). Emphasize scientific significance and reviewer-relevant strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and number of awards / award purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The program will support over 80 early career researchers for five years at U.S. academic institutions, DOE national laboratories, and Office of Science user facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware the program funds a limited number of multi-year awards focused on supporting outstanding early career scientists; competitiveness is high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find program announcement and supplemental information
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research topics must fall within the programmatic priorities of DOE’s Office of Science, which are provided in the program announcement. Further information can be found on the Office of Science funding opportunities page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the full program announcement on the Office of Science funding opportunities page for detailed submission requirements, review criteria, formatting, and other mandatory instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission informational webinar
rubrics_metrics.description: A webinar on this opportunity will be held on November 30th at 3 p.m. EST. Please register here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend or review materials from the webinar to clarify program expectations, timelines, and Q&A; register in advance as directed.
